repo_notes.content: Local benchmark suite for LLMs (German project, English code). Goal: reproducible local benchmarks on an NVIDIA RTX 5060 Ti with 16 GB VRAM, finding the Pareto frontier of parameter count, GGUF quantization, KV-cache/context settings and parallel execution. Python 3.12 is the supported runtime. Since v13.0.6 all production Python modules live in src/; document src/, tests/, doc-git/ and the versioned workflow files, while treating unrelated root-level legacy scripts as non-canonical.
repo_notes.author: pskraemer11

repo_notes.content: Configuration is data-driven and lives in doc-git/: model_registry.yaml is the source of truth for benchmark metadata and provider-neutral runtime policy (quantization, benchmark context, sampling, reasoning, blueprint and template policy); blueprint_definitions.yaml defines prompt blueprints and doc-git/Jinja-Chat-Templates contains explicit templates. GGUF headers are the source of truth for immutable technical facts such as architecture and native context limits. LM Studio JSON files are backend-local artifacts, never the global source of truth. registry_tool.py commands sync/compare/validate/rm and validate --ci are the main maintenance entrypoints.
repo_notes.author: pskraemer11

repo_notes.content: Key workflow: discover local GGUFs and provider models, resolve them against model_registry.yaml, read GGUF headers for technical identity, then run registry_tool.py sync/validate and a selected benchmark run-spec. The shared BLACKLIST excludes embeddings, OCR, vision-only, whisper and other unsupported auxiliary models; companion files such as MTP drafters, mmproj and importance matrices are not standalone benchmark models.
repo_notes.author: pskraemer11

repo_notes.content: Current architecture to document explicitly: Benchmark Runner depends on provider-neutral InferenceClient (chat/completions/models), ModelManager (list/load/unload/current) and ModelRegistry (metadata, sampling, reasoning, quantization and context). Providers include LM Studio, TabbyAPI, generic OpenAI-compatible endpoints, authenticated Unsloth Studio and a runner-managed Unsloth llama-server process. The runner must not depend on LM Studio for generic inference.
repo_notes.author: pskraemer11

repo_notes.content: Testing and delivery: tests live under tests/ and run with Python 3.12 via pytest. validate --ci is a headless registry check without LM Studio, local hub state or local GGUF inventory. Versioned .githooks/ provide staged pre-commit checks, conventional commit-msg validation and a complete pre-push review gate; CI and Review workflows independently repeat the relevant checks with UTF-8 output and a focused mypy scope.
repo_notes.author: pskraemer11

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: Project purpose: reproducible local LLM benchmarking under 16 GB VRAM constraints on an RTX 5060 Ti. Summarize the four pipelines (Custom, EvalPlus, LM-Eval, Agentic), the provider-neutral runner architecture, and the supported coding, reasoning, knowledge and agentic benchmark families.

pages.title: Getting Started & Installation
pages.purpose: Clone github.com/pskraemer11/Local-LLM-Benchmark-Tool, install Python 3.12 dependencies, then select a backend through LLM_PROVIDER. LM Studio >=1.4.1 with its REST/OpenAI API is one supported provider; TabbyAPI, OpenAI-compatible endpoints and the local Unsloth llama-server provider are alternatives. Explain that local GGUF discovery and registry validation are separate from inference-server selection.

pages.title: Source Layout (src/)
pages.purpose: Describe the current source layout: src/run_benchmarks.py as launcher, src/model_manager.py as provider facade, src/model_registry.py as runtime resolver, src/providers/ for LM Studio, TabbyAPI, OpenAI-compatible and Unsloth implementations, src/local_model_resolver.py for local GGUF inventory, plus registry, blueprint, benchmark and result modules. Cover tests/, doc-git/ and versioned .githooks/ as operationally relevant areas.

pages.title: Model Registry & Registration

pages.title: Blueprints & System Prompts

pages.title: Benchmark Pipelines

List the corresponding src/ modules and how they are launched.

pages.title: Reasoning & Thinking Mode
